text:
Samir Qureshi: Question for LTS cut (1.18-lts). Do we want to keep the experimental batching heuristic that landed in 1.18 main? It’s currently on by default for some routes. I’m leaning we disable/guard it on LTS to reduce surprise variance.

Sofia Ivanova: +1 to being cautious. That heuristic touches scheduler behavior (queue coalescing + dynamic microbatch size). It’s not a “bug fix”, it’s a behavior change. LTS should bias for predictability.

Marcus Reed: I pulled numbers from perf-canary for the heuristic ON vs OFF on the release branch candidate from yesterday. Summary (A100-80GB, 7B + 13B mix, mixed prompt length dist):
- p50 latency: +0.3% (noise)
- p95 latency: +4.8% worse with heuristic ON (mostly long-tail on burst)
- throughput (tok/s): +2.1% better with heuristic ON
On H100, the delta is smaller but still p95 swings around (+3-4%) depending on prompt length distribution. It’s also noisier.

Connor O'Brien: For LTS, I’d rather take the small throughput hit than risk p95 regressions. Dedicated customers tend to pin and care about tails + stability.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel side: no direct kernel changes, but the heuristic can change effective batch composition which shifts which fused path gets hit. That’s where the variance comes from (esp. when requests bunch up then drain). I don’t love it being default on LTS.

Allison Grant: From SRE POV: if we ship LTS with something that changes p95 behavior under burst, we’ll spend patch weeks arguing “is it real or benchmark noise” and then firefighting customer escalations. We already have enough moving pieces (perf gates, runner contention).

Noah Patel: Is there a way to keep it in LTS but behind an explicit config flag, default OFF? That gives us an escape hatch for customers who want the extra throughput and are willing to validate.

Sofia Ivanova: That’s what I’d recommend: default OFF for LTS, documented as opt-in. Also ensures backports don’t accidentally re-enable it via merge drift.

Leila Farouk: QA note: we don’t have enough coverage around edge-case queueing scenarios for that heuristic (mixed streaming + non-streaming, cancellations, etc). We can add tests, but not in time for first LTS patch.

Samir Qureshi: Any known correctness issues? Or purely perf/variance concern.

Sofia Ivanova: No known correctness bug, but it changes admission + batch sizing under pressure. That’s “behavioral correctness” for some customers (e.g., they interpret tail behavior as SLO violations).

Marcus Reed: One more data point: on the “bursty traffic” synthetic (spike from 50 rps -> 250 rps for 90s) we saw occasional scheduler backlog oscillation w/ heuristic ON. It recovers, but p95 spikes by ~9-12% during the spike window. OFF keeps it flatter.

Connor O'Brien: That’s enough for me. LTS policy should be: experimental heuristics disabled unless they’re required to fix Sev1 correctness.

Hiro Tanaka: Agree. Also, if we have to debug perf regressions for LTS customers, removing variables is key.

Noah Patel: OK, so: LTS default OFF, main stays ON? Or also move to default OFF in main?

Sofia Ivanova: Mainline decision can be separate. For LTS, default OFF. For main, we can keep iterating and improve stability.

Allison Grant: +1 separate. LTS is the “slow lane”.

Samir Qureshi: I’ll open/track a PR on the LTS branch to disable it (or gate behind `RUNTIME_EXPERIMENTAL_BATCHING=1`). We should add a line in LTS release notes: “Experimental batching heuristic disabled by default to improve tail latency predictability; opt-in flag available.”

Connor O'Brien: Please link it here when up. Also add perf notes + rationale to make it easy for Support/CS.

Marcus Reed: If you want, I can attach the perf-canary run IDs + graphs so we have evidence for the release notes + any future debates.

Samir Qureshi: yes please.

Marcus Reed: Links:
- perf-canary summary: https://github.com/redwood/perf-canary/actions/runs/ (run id 118421 / 118439)
- p95 comparison screenshot in thread: https://redwood-internal/perf/compare?branch=runtime-1.18-lts&metric=p95
(you might need VPN)

Leila Farouk: Suggest adding a small regression test to ensure the LTS default remains OFF (config snapshot test), so a future cherry-pick doesn’t flip it.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. Also document the flag location (env var + helm value + private installer config) so customers can control it explicitly.

Samir Qureshi: Great. I’ll do:
1) disable by default on LTS branch
2) keep opt-in flag
3) add config test
4) add release note snippet

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: This matches the LTS spirit. If any customer asks “why is throughput lower vs main”, we can point to tail stability and the opt-in path.

Allison Grant: :+1: Please ping me when it’s merged; I’ll note it for SLO dashboards so we don’t compare apples-to-oranges when pilot customers switch to LTS.

Samir Qureshi: Will do.

Hiro Tanaka: One more: make sure the flag name is explicit “experimental” so it doesn’t become de-facto required config in enterprise deployments.

Sofia Ivanova: +100. “experimental” in the name + documented as not covered by LTS perf guarantees.

Connor O'Brien: Cool. Decision: disable experimental batching heuristic on LTS by default; keep opt-in behind explicit flag; document + add guard test.

Samir Qureshi: Ack, proceeding.
